content: The text provided appears to be a long list of references from scientific and medical studies, primarily focused on the treatment of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, including co-infections with HIV, using various antiviral therapies. 1. High sustained virologic response (SVR) rates were observed in treatment-naïve patients with chronic HCV infection and HIV/HCV co-infection, as presented at the 67th Annual Meeting of the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) in 2016. 2. Ishigami M., Hayashi K., Honda T., et al. reported real-world data on the efficacy of daclatasvir and asunaprevir combination therapy for HCV genotype 1b infection in patients with renal dysfunction. This study was published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology in 2017. 3. Itoh Y., Suzuki F., Karino Y., et al. investigated the prevalence and impact of baseline resistance-associated variants on the efficacy of elbasvir/grazoprevir in Japanese patients with HCV genotype 1 infection. These findings were presented at the 67th AASLD Liver Meeting in 2016. 4. Iwamoto M., Sonderup M., Fortas C., Maman D. evaluated the real-world effectiveness and safety of daclatasvir/sofosbuvir ± ribavirin in patients with HCV genotypes 5 and 6, as part of a study conducted by Médecins Sans Frontières in 2017. 5. Jacobson I., Brau N., Bourgeois S., et al. conducted an integrated safety analysis of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) for 12 weeks in over 1,000 patients treated in the ASTRAL-1, ASTRAL-2, and ASTRAL-3 studies. This was presented at the 51st Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) in 2016. 6. Jacobson I.M., Yoshida E.M., Sulkowski M., et al. demonstrated that treatment with sofosbuvir and ribavirin for 12 weeks achieved an SVR12 rate of 78% in genotype 2/3 patients who were interferon-ineligible, intolerant, or unwilling. These results were from the Phase 3 POSITRON trial, published in Journal of Hepatology in 2013. 7. Jacobson I.M., Lawitz E., Gane E.J., et al. assessed the efficacy of an 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir in patients with chronic HCV infection through two Phase 3 randomized trials, published in Gastroenterology in 2017. 8. Jargalsaikhan G., Dashtseren B., Dendev B., et al. compared active versus passive follow-up examination of patients with chronic hepatitis C during sofosbuvir/ledipasvir treatment. This study was presented in Journal of Hepatology in 2017. 9. Ji D., Chen G.F., Wang C., et al. evaluated a 12-week ribavirin-free direct-acting antiviral regimen for treatment-experienced Chinese patients with HCV genotype 1b infection, including those with cirrhosis. The findings were published in Hepatology International in 2016. 10. Johnson S.W., Ammirati S.R., Hartis C.E., et al. examined the effectiveness of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir in real-world patients with chronic hepatitis C using a collaborative treatment approach, published in International Journal of Antimicrobial Agents in 2017. 11. Kao J.H., Lee Y.J., Heo J., et al. conducted a sub-analysis of the HALLMARK DUAL study, focusing on the efficacy of all-oral daclatasvir plus asunaprevir for chronic HCV genotype 1b infection in Asian patients. The results were published in Liver International in 2016. 12. Kao J.H., Peng C.Y., Chang T.T., et al. evaluated dual therapy with daclatasvir and asunaprevir in Korean and Taiwanese patients with HCV genotype 1b infection, published in Hepatology International. 13. Karino Y., Suzuki F., Suzuki Y., et al. compared the all-oral dual combination of daclatasvir plus asunaprevir with telaprevir plus peginterferon alfa and ribavirin in treatment-naïve Japanese patients with chronic HCV genotype 1b infection. This Phase 3 study was published in Hepatology International. 14. Kattakuzhy S., Emmanuel B., Gross C., et al. found that adherence to prescriptions was a better predictor of SVR than adherence to treatment visits among patients treated with direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy in a task-shifting model. This was presented in Journal of Hepatology in 2017. 15. Kawada N., Suzuki F., Karino Y., et al. evaluated the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of grazoprevir (MK-5172) and elbasvir (MK-8742) in non-cirrhotic Japanese patients with HCV genotype 1 infection. This Phase 2 study was published in Hepatology in 2015. 16. Kawakami Y., Imamura M., Ikeda H., et al. conducted a pilot study on the pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety of daclatasvir plus asunaprevir in dialysis patients with chronic hepatitis C, published in Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2016. 17. Pang P., Polis M., Kottilil S. demonstrated the efficacy of ledipasvir and sofosbuvir for HCV genotype 4 in a proof-of-concept, single-center, open-label Phase 2a cohort study, published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2015. 18. Meissner E.G., Barrett L., Marti M., et al. reported virological response after a 6-week triple-drug regimen for hepatitis C in a proof-of-concept Phase 2a cohort study, published in The Lancet in 2015. 19. Korenaga M., Izumi N., Yokosuka O., et al. found that sustained virologic response (SVR) achieved with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir reduced the incidence of hepatocellular carcinoma in Japanese patients with HCV genotype 1 infection, compared to simeprevir with peginterferon plus ribavirin. This was presented in Journal of Hepatology in 2017. 20. Kottilil S., Wyles D., Brau N., et al. evaluated the fixed-dose combination of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir for 12 weeks in patients co-infected with HCV and HIV-1 in the Phase 3 ASTRAL-5 study, presented at the 26th Annual Conference of the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) in 2017. This format provides a clear, professional summary of each study while maintaining the technical details and context.
